scorecard.note: Strengthen the payoff so the ending directly answers the hook’s promise and gives a clear, memorable takeaway.

storyboard.ears: Men are losing their sperm, and the drop is getting faster.
In 1973, the average count was 101. By 2018 it was under half that, establishing the long decline.
storyboard.eyes: substance: swimming sperm cells; cause: Data turns the microscope's stage wheel, sliding the 1973 sample out and the 2018 sample in
storyboard.evidence: Human Reproduction Update | Average sperm concentration, 1973 vs 2018 (million per mL) | https://academic.oup.com/humupd/article/29/2/157/6932384 | 2026-11-05

storyboard.ears: Since 2000, counts fall 2.6% a year, more than double the old pace. The same decline is accelerating.
storyboard.evidence: Human Reproduction Update | Annual rate of sperm count decline, before vs after 2000 (percent per year) | https://academic.oup.com/humupd/article/29/2/157/6932384 | 2026-11-05

storyboard.ears: That acceleration reaches the whole sample: total sperm count fell 62%, not just the concentration.
storyboard.eyes: substance: milky white sample fluid; cause: Data pulls the jar's tap lever down and the milky sample pours out into the sink
storyboard.evidence: Human Reproduction Update | Decline in sperm concentration vs total sperm count, 1973-2018 (percent) | https://academic.oup.com/humupd/article/29/2/157/6932384 | 2026-11-05

storyboard.ears: The decline now affects both concentration and total output, raising the stakes for future families.
